To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Lebanese and Beninese importers of used cars are different because they are involved in different types of transnational trade.

Lebanese and Beninese transnational entrepreneurs engaged in second-hand car import–export trade differ in terms of their social networks, the level of trust between them and their ability to circulate between the two continents.
Lebanese car importers, operating within a trade diaspora in Cotonou, are able to rely upon other Lebanese to send their second-hand cars from Europe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of trust in the organisation and management of transnational trade activities.
the relationship between the mobility and social capital of Lebanese and Beninese cross-border entrepreneurs engaged in second-hand car import–export between Europe and West-Africa.
how the social capital of the car importers, and the way they mobilise it, is linked to their ability to operate in a transnational trade and to their spatial mobility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Lebanese and Beninese importers of second hand cars have a different relationship with mobility and social capital.

the Lebanese car importers are able to operate in a more efficient way than their Beninese counterparts because they can mobilise social capital, a concept that has been defined by Bourdieu (1980) as the sum of actual or potential resources that can be used by an actor to obtain an advantage for himself in a field of exchange.
Lebanese and Beninese traders are not equally able to take advantage of the opportunities that the transnational second-hand car business offers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Lebanese entrepreneurs have been able to build trust and to create a diaspora that allows them to operate in a context of low risk.

, in the second-hand car trade, the Lebanese are able to create a trust-based network of business relationships, which enables them to operate in a more efficient way and thus gain a competitive advantage over Beninese importers.
the Lebanese car importers are more mobile than the Beninese ones, but that the Beninese ones are more entrepreneurial.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ability to mobilise social capital, in the form of trust, is crucial to the success of transnational entrepreneurs.
trust is the key factor in explaining the differences between the Lebanese and Beninese importers.
the ability to recreate trust is a major factor in the development of transnational trade.
